title: DOW-UAP-D48, Department of the Air Force Report, 1996
doc_notes: This document is a technical report from the Research Triangle Institute to the U.S. Air Force regarding the modeling of space-booster failure responses for risk calculations, containing historical failure narratives in the appendices. / This document is a technical report from the Department of the Air Force (RTI) dated September 1996, detailing launch failure modes and performance histories for Atlas, Delta, Titan, and Thor vehicles. / This report documents historical launch failure modes for Atlas, Delta, and Titan launch vehicles, providing detailed narratives for anomalies and failures between 1957 and 1996.

incidents.summary: Atlas 8E launch failure resulting in loss of stability and impact 1316 miles downrange and 215 miles crossrange.
incidents.quote: Missile stability was lost at about 161 seconds

incidents.summary: Titan M-4 launch failure resulting in impact 86 miles short and 14 miles right of target.
incidents.quote: A one-bit error in the W velocity accumulation caused impact 86 miles short and 14 miles right of target.

incidents.summary: Atlas 145D launch failure involving erroneous guidance commands and abnormal maneuvers.
incidents.quote: Due to this and faulty guidance equations, erroneous guidance commands were given based on invalid rate data.

incidents.summary: Atlas SLV-3 launch failure resulting in loss of pitch control and abnormal attitude.
incidents.quote: Vehicle became unstable when B2 pitch control was lost at 121 seconds.

incidents.summary: Atlas 95F launch failure resulting in erratic yaw and roll rates and destruct.
incidents.quote: Immediately after liftoff the telemetered roll and yaw rates indicated that the missile was erratic.

incidents.summary: Delta Intelsat III launch failure involving undamped pitch oscillations and violent maneuvers.
incidents.quote: Due to loss of rate gyro, undamped pitch oscillations began at 20 seconds.

incidents.summary: Delta Pioneer E launch failure involving hydraulic system failure and tumble.
incidents.quote: First-stage hydraulics system failed a few seconds before first-stage burnout (MECO).

incidents.summary: Atlas 68E launch failure resulting in loss of attitude control and retrofire mode.
incidents.quote: As a result, attitude control was lost and the thrusting sustainer pivoted the missile to a retrofire attitude

incidents.summary: Prospector (Joust) launch failure involving radical pitch-up maneuver.
incidents.quote: The vehicle made a radical pitch-up maneuver due to aft-skirt structural failure at approximately T+14 Seconds.

incidents.summary: Red Tigress sounding rocket launch failure involving near 90-degree right turn.
incidents.quote: Within a second or two after clearing the launcher, the rocket made a near 90° right turn

incidents.summary: Atlas 4A launch failure due to fuel supply drop to B2 engine, leading to thrust asymmetry and destruction by safety officer.
incidents.explanation: Drop in fuel supply to B2 engine.
incidents.quote: drop in fuel supply to B2 engine produced a drop in performance and shutdown

incidents.summary: Atlas 6A launch failure due to loss of LOX regulator in booster gas generator.
incidents.explanation: Loss of LOX regulator in the booster gas generator.
incidents.quote: Loss of thrust was due to loss of LOX regulator in the booster gas generator.

incidents.summary: Atlas 13A launch failure due to B2 turbopump/engine failure and aerodynamic heating.
incidents.explanation: B2 turbopump failure and shorting of vernier engine feedback transducer.
incidents.quote: Failure was attributed to shorting of a vernier engine feedback transducer due to aerodynamic heating.

incidents.summary: Atlas 11A launch failure due to flight control system component failure.
incidents.explanation: Probable component failure in flight control system.
incidents.quote: Probable cause of oscillation was a component failure in flight control system.

incidents.summary: Atlas 15A launch failure due to B1 turbopump failure.
incidents.explanation: B1 turbopump failure.
incidents.quote: Booster engines shut down prematurely at 105.3 seconds due to B1 turbopump failure.

incidents.summary: Atlas booster fuel-pump pressure dropped due to a fuel pre-valve failure, booster lost thrust, fell back on launch pad, and was destroyed.
incidents.explanation: fuel pre-valve failure
incidents.quote: booster lost thrust, fell back on launch pad, and was destroyed

incidents.summary: Booster gas-generator loop failure resulted in decreasing performance, explosion in thrust section, and vehicle breakup.
incidents.explanation: failure in the booster gas-generator loop
incidents.quote: failure in the booster gas-generator loop resulted in decreasing booster performance

incidents.summary: Circuit board failure caused sustainer shutdown at BECO; Agena ignition created wild uprange movements on IP display.
incidents.explanation: circuit board failure caused by excessive vibrations
incidents.quote: creating wild uprange movements on the IP display

incidents.summary: Agena engine shut down after one second; helium pressurization system continued until tanks burst.
incidents.explanation: Agena startup failure
incidents.quote: Propellants ceased flowing but the helium pressurization system continued to pressurize the propellant tanks until they burst.

incidents.summary: Missile spiraling due to hydraulic system failure during staging; telemetry indicated rapidly varying pitch, roll, and yaw rates.
behavior: varying pitch, roll, and yaw rates
incidents.explanation: hydraulic system failure
incidents.quote: skyscreen operator reported that vehicle was spiraling

incidents.summary: Reentry vehicle impacted 82 miles beyond target when head suppression valve failed to close at SECO.
incidents.explanation: head suppression valve failed to close
incidents.quote: reentry vehicle impacted 82 miles beyond the target point

incidents.summary: Centaur engines started but one could not maintain thrust, resulting in tumbling and fuel starvation.
incidents.explanation: thrust imbalance
incidents.quote: Thrust imbalance resulted in tumbling, followed by fuel starvation

incidents.summary: Sustainer pitch-actuator feedback-loop failed; roll and pitch rates increased; vehicle stability lost.
incidents.explanation: sustainer pitch-actuator feedback-loop failed open
incidents.quote: sustainer pitch-actuator feedback-loop failed open

incidents.explanation: B2 pitch control was lost
incidents.quote: Vehicle became unstable when B2 pitch control was lost

incidents.summary: Reentry vehicle undershot target by 20 miles due to vernier engine shutdown caused by helium pressure decay.
incidents.explanation: abnormal decay of control-bottle helium pressure
incidents.quote: reentry vehicle undershot the target by 20 miles

incidents.summary: Missile appeared to lose thrust and breakup; major pieces impacted 32 to 40 miles downrange.
incidents.explanation: unknown

incidents.summary: Diverging roll oscillations, tumbling, and breakup of vehicle.
incidents.explanation: anomalous events early in flight
incidents.quote: Diverging roll oscillations actually began about 21.4 seconds

incidents.summary: Missile erratic immediately after liftoff, yawed hard left then right, pitched up violently, and destructed.
incidents.explanation: unknown
incidents.quote: Immediately after liftoff the telemetered roll and yaw rates indicated that the missile was erratic.

incidents.summary: Missile lost attitude control, executing a hard yaw rate turn.
incidents.explanation: unknown
incidents.quote: The missile then lost attitude control, executing a hard yaw rate turn

incidents.summary: Sustainer engine shut down prematurely; destruct sent.
incidents.explanation: unknown
incidents.quote: sustainer engine shut down prematurely

incidents.summary: Pitch stabilization lost; vehicle began accelerated nose-down tumbling motion.
incidents.explanation: failure of the rate gyro or electrical failure

incidents.summary: Sustainer engine turbine damage resulted in hot gas leaks and vehicle breakup.
incidents.explanation: Sustainer engine turbine damage

incidents.quote: flight-control avionics was unable to maintain vehicle stability

incidents.summary: Breakup resulted from external explosion in flame bucket; radar reported multiple pieces.
incidents.explanation: external explosion in the flame bucket
incidents.quote: breakup apparently resulted from an external explosion in the flame bucket

incidents.summary: Leak in booster hot-gas generator resulted in fire and violent maneuver; vehicle exploded.
incidents.explanation: leak in the booster hot-gas generator
incidents.quote: The vehicle went into a violent maneuver at 54.9 seconds

incidents.summary: Asymmetric thrust caused yaw and roll rates; attitude control lost; vehicle breakup.
incidents.explanation: lube oil pressure on B2 booster engine dropped
incidents.quote: Asymmetric thrust during shutdown caused yaw and roll rates

incidents.summary: Thrust performance decayed; missile pitched over and impacted ground behind launch pad.
incidents.explanation: plugging of the gas-generator fuel-cooling parts
incidents.quote: pitched over to the right, and travel horizontally for about one second

incidents.summary: Vehicle struck by lightning; guidance computer commanded hard right turn; breakup.
incidents.explanation: struck by lightning
incidents.quote: when the vehicle was struck by lightning

incidents.summary: Turbo-machinery decelerated and stopped; thrust imbalance; vehicle tumbled out of control.
incidents.explanation: air entering through stuck-open check valve liquefied and froze in LH2 pump
incidents.quote: Due to the resulting thrust imbalance, the vehicle tumbled out of control.

incidents.summary: Centaur engine check valve stuck open; air froze in LH2 pump; thrust imbalance; destruct sent.
incidents.explanation: Centaur engine check valve stuck open
incidents.quote: A Centaur engine check valve stuck open allowing air into the turbopumps.
